recommended.why: auto takes the Steel 64-row micro-batch: 1.42-1.56x prefill over the per-token loop; its KL against per-token is 2.55e-3 to 3.94e-3, a hundred times the dense arm, which is why this family's class is moe_kl

the batched routed half pays at 32 or more slots: re-measured 2026-10-29 at +53.2% prefill on auto/96 slots (1.54x, against the recorded 1.65x) while 16 slots now reads inside the floor; it is opt-in until its default owes the seam-on probe, the memory oracle, Ornith and a second chip
auto resolves to 96 slots on this host, which is where the routed batch pays; 16 slots keeps the footprint near 1.6 GiB at the cost of prefill
default on; qwen_moe_chunked_refusal names the reasons it falls back (hadamard, the read-overlap seam, an open drafter), and capabilities reports the conditional
JIT warmup stays opt-in: docs/MOE_STARTUP.md measured the startup cost it moves and decided the default

sweeps.description: the routed batch reading the next sub-batch's experts while the GPU runs the previous one
sweeps.note: the arms carry no slot count: run it with --slots 64 and again at --slots auto. At 32 slots and below a sub-batch can hold every slot the next one needs, the read-ahead mostly falls back, and the candidate reads as dirty (no [engaged] routed_batch_overlap)

findings.workload: tslab profile, protocol long-synthesis, 16 decode, routed_batch=1 at 16, 32 and 64 streamed slots and auto (96); 2 clean rounds each
findings.conditions: medians of 2 clean runs per arm; the auto arm's warmup was dirty (corespotlightd), its measured runs clean
findings.note: the routed batch ran each sub-batch's pread and its GPU work strictly in series, so up to the routed GPU busy time (about 1.65 ms of 7.8 ms per token at auto) was recoverable by reading ahead. The union cap is 32, so 64 slots and up hold two unions and the read-ahead costs no sub-batch width; at 32 it would halve the cap and at 16 it cannot work

findings.workload: tslab sweep routed_overlap, protocol long-synthesis, 16 decode; batched (routed_batch=1) against ahead (routed_batch=1, routed_batch_overlap=1), once at 64 streamed slots and once at auto (96); 3 clean pairs each, 0 dirty, order alternating by round
findings.conditions: no null calibration ran first, so the floor was the 2% minimum. Every ahead run printed [engaged] routed_batch_overlap. Both arms' prefill-logits and decode digests were identical in every run at both slot counts, the bit-exact claim on the real install. The 64-slot sweep is experiment routed-overlap-s64-2026-10-26, record 1793073705405-9753-17
findings.note: the auto result recovers most of the routed GPU busy time the profile put on the table. Not a default: it rides TURBOSPARK_ROUTED_BATCH, which owes its own gates first (seam-on probe, memory oracle, Ornith, a second chip)

findings.conditions: the verdict field is the routed_batch@96 WIN; prefill_arm verdicts 1793278899487-99475-63 (scalar LOSS) and 1793278899491-99475-64 (per_token LOSS); slots verdicts -99475-110/111/112 (s16/s32 LOSS, s64 NOISE); sweep records -99475-32, -65, -113; prefill null floor 0.45% (-67131-16), decode 0.90% (-7472802-89542-16); moe_kl; memory passed everywhere except the by-design slot-cache growth
findings.note: re-confirms every standing verdict on the current build: routed_batch pays at auto/96 slots (1.54x here against the recorded 1.65x - same direction, ~12 points smaller) and does NOT pay at 16 (now inside the floor, against the recorded +2.5%); Steel stays the prefill default; auto/96 stays the decode winner with s64 tied at 2.3 GiB less peak; the read_overlap arm still refuses under chunked prefill (the seam condition, record 1793279138753-99475-118)

a byte-identical M-row GDN path for the batched prefill

no drafter install of this family exists here; the MTP flow is wired but unmeasured

how concentrated routing really is on this install: tslab expert-census gives the share of selections in experts used 17+ times per batch (28.75% on one 2026-10-21 capture), the union per full batch against 16/32/64/96 slots, and the routed sub-batch sizes per cap; the slots sweep above should be read beside it

whether MoE prefill is compute bound yet: tslab profile prints the moe_bound class per phase; the Neural Engine expert idea stays closed until prefill reads compute_bound (docs/SPEEDUP_PLAYBOOK.md, Not pursued)
traps: declare moe_kl, never dense_kl, for a KL-bounded change on this family: the batched arm's KL is a hundred times the dense arm's
